Would paid deepfakes lead to greater repressive blowback than free deepfakes? Not necessarily. It's my impression (not a lawyer) that LEO and courts take illegal moneymaking activities more seriously than illegal free activities, partly because the "perpetrators" seem less sympathetic. This is doubly so with civil law where sanctions and sometimes liability are linked to presumed profit lost for violations. This is true in copyright cases - plaintiffs have to claim the offender has cost them sales or somesuch, which is why it's easier to prosecute a paid derivative site than a free derivative site. High-profile public sites selling deepfake services would be obvious targets for LEO campaigns and provide test cases for laws which could then be used against free creators. The other problem here is that some people would almost certainly try to order deepfakes of non-celebrities which would then be used in harassment, fraud, blackmail and so on. Some sellers would almost certainly be prepared to do this. And at this point, the entire site might become liable for conspiracy. At the very least, the reputation of the community would be further harmed. But whatever the method they use, someone who makes deepfake of their ex based on a faceset of photos only they possess is likely to get caught, particularly if they use them for insidious means. This doesn't necessarily mean the seller will be caught but just that the fact that they "paid for deepfake services on the darknet" would be in the news.

Certainly the makers of the porn (and sometimes the videos from which the facesets are taken) could allege copyright violation and issue takedown notices. The media's trying to frame deepfakes as a "consent violation" but they'd have difficulty pushing this under current law anywhere (why is a deepfake different from a photoshopped image or a hand-drawn cartoon in this regard?) They can try in any jurisdiction in America for online content, and if they can convince a jury in a conservative community that deepfakes are offensive, they could get convictions.
